result:
Good — this was running against the full project's `*AgentTest.java` set (just mine exists) and confirms the single failure.

I wrote `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/csv/CSVFormatAgentTest.java` with 75 tests covering `CSVFormat` and `CSVFormat.Builder` (defaults, validation of delimiter/quote/escape/comment-marker/duplicate-header-mode, header handling from arrays/enum/`ResultSet`/`ResultSetMetaData` via Mockito, `validate()` consistency rules, `equals`/`hashCode`/`toString`, printing/quoting behavior for all `QuoteMode`s, null-string handling, multi-char delimiters, and deprecated `with*` methods).

74 tests pass. One fails and shows a real bug:

- **`testWithRecordSeparatorRejectsInvalidString`**: `CSVFormat.withRecordSeparator(String)` (and the underlying `Builder.setRecordSeparator(String)`) is documented (`@throws IllegalArgumentException if recordSeparator is none of CR, LF or CRLF`) to reject any record separator that isn't CR, LF, or CRLF, but the implementation performs no such validation at all — any arbitrary string is silently accepted.
